channel_diagnostic.description: The UVFITS stores one channel per IF. Page 2 replots marker centers from the NN–PV page of the rPICARD spectrum, one scan-level value per channel and hand. The plot coordinates give approximate amplitudes and phases; channel frequencies match the observation grid. Rings mark all channels with RR above 2× and LL above 1.5× their respective within-IF median amplitudes. Three coincide with the final channel (115) of SPWs 3, 8 and 24. The largest RR peak is at 227.626789 GHz (24/115), about 7.4× its IF median. Features A and B also contain peaks at 11/41 and 28/97. At 28/97, RL is about 3.8× its median. Both cross-hands also spike at the three last-channel peaks. In IF 28, RR stays elevated across much of the window as well as spiking at channel 97.
channel_diagnostic.command_note: These optional channel selections target the original 116-channel windows. Use a working copy whose station names, SPW IDs and channel grid match the observation log. The example filename is a placeholder. The local data support checking the frequencies and indices; these commands have not been executed on the original MS. Compare other baselines before expanding any selection to NN or PV alone. At each circled peak, a cross-hand is included if its amplitude also exceeds its window median by three robust standard deviations (1.4826 × MAD).
commands:
flagdata(vis='channelized_working_copy.ms', mode='manual', field='M87', antenna='NN&PV',
         scan='2', spw='3:115', correlation='RR,LL,RL,LR')

flagdata(vis='channelized_working_copy.ms', mode='manual', field='M87', antenna='NN&PV',
         scan='2', spw='8:115', correlation='RR,LL,RL,LR')

flagdata(vis='channelized_working_copy.ms', mode='manual', field='M87', antenna='NN&PV',
         scan='2', spw='11:41', correlation='RR,LL')

flagdata(vis='channelized_working_copy.ms', mode='manual', field='M87', antenna='NN&PV',
         scan='2', spw='24:115', correlation='RR,LL,RL,LR')

flagdata(vis='channelized_working_copy.ms', mode='manual', field='M87', antenna='NN&PV',
         scan='2', spw='28:97', correlation='RR,LL,RL')

notes.title: Early loss of coherent amplitude
notes.body: The first positive weights occur at 25.6 s. From 25–64 s the median 4 s amplitudes are 0.018 (RR) and 0.017 (LL) on the plotted scale. After 72 s they are 0.876 and 0.795. The shared recovery is abrupt. The amber band marks the conservative candidate interval. The transition from 64–72 s is left for review.

notes.title: What the individual integrations show
notes.body: From 25–64 s, only 18% of valid RR samples and 18% of LL samples lie within 30° of zero phase. From 72 s onward, the fractions rise to 96% and 95%. The early median individual amplitude is 0.205 for both hands on the plotted scale. The much smaller coherent means on page 1 reflect cancellation among samples with widely dispersed phases.

notes.title: A  ·  226.836 GHz, IF 11
notes.body: Relative to the mean of the two adjacent IF amplitudes, RR is 21% higher and LL is 11% lower. Their phases deviate by about −6° and +5° from the adjacent complex mean. This smaller feature merits comparison with other baselines before flagging.

notes.title: B  ·  227.832 GHz, IF 28
notes.body: RR reaches 2.23 times its adjacent-IF amplitude and shifts −23° in phase. RL reaches 2.25 times its neighbors. From 72–156 s and 156–240 s, RR stays above 2.1 times and RL above 1.8 times their neighbors. The recurrence supports a candidate for both products. The channel spectrum on page 2 shows the structure within this IF.

notes.title: Antenna attribution and phase
notes.body: A single baseline cannot distinguish NN from PV. RR and RL share R at the first station in the plotted UVFITS orientation, making NN R worth checking on independent baselines. Outside the localized features, RR/LL phase stays near zero across frequency. The weaker cross-hands show greater phase scatter.

command_note: Run only on a working Measurement Set imported from this UVFITS with matching station and SPW mappings. Both selections were tested in order with CASA 6.6.6 on a disposable import of just this baseline and scan. The changed flags matched the intended cells exactly: 6,144 in the first call and 976 additional cells in the second.
commands:
flagdata(vis='M87_calibrated.ms', mode='manual', field='M87', antenna='NN&PV',
         timerange='2026/03/17/03:11:00~2026/03/17/03:15:00', spw='28:0', correlation='RR,RL')
